subject: Privacy Annex / Data Processing Annex — redlines, evidence request, DocuSign path
messages:
From: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@helixhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Brooks <oliver.brooks@helixhealth.com>, Helix Privacy <privacy@helixhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-12 09:12 AM PDT
Subject: Privacy Annex — initial redlines and questions

Sean —

Thanks for sending over your standard DPA. Attached is Helix's redline (Helix_DPA_Redlines_v1.docx) with a few high-level items we need to resolve before we can move to legal execution:

- Subprocessors: we proposed a carve-out for subprocessors used for analytics (Section 3.2). Need confirmation on your notice cadence and objection process.
- International transfers: we redlined to require SCCs + an explicit EU-US addendum.
- Retention: Helix prefers a 5-year retention cap for customer data, with shorter periods for logs; your template references "reasonable" — please propose a numeric cap.
- Audit evidence: we will need a recent SOC 2 Type II, plus a current subprocessor inventory and last-12-months penetration test summary.
- E-sign/Execution: please confirm whether you prefer DocuSign or AdobeSign — Helix requires DocuSign-by-default.

We are aiming to get a counter by COB 10/14 so internal counsel can clear. Happy to set a 30-minute sync if that helps.

Thanks,
Emma Sullivan
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Governance
Helix Health

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12 11:05 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Privacy Annex — initial redlines and questions

Emma —

Appreciate the clear redline. Quick response to the bullets while we get privacy counsel looped in (cc'd):

- Subprocessors: Redwood provides a 30-day notice for new subprocessors and allows customers to object on reasonable security grounds; if not resolved, we offer a mitigation path (migration window or limited-scope carveout). We'll confirm whether analytics infra falls under the standard list or is an opt-in.
- Transfers: We publish the standard SCCs + we can sign an EU-US addendum. Monica, please confirm language / any additional controls.
- Retention: Our template uses purpose-based retention; we can propose a numeric default of 7 years for primary records with shorter windows for logs (90 days) — willing to discuss 5 years if Helix has regulatory constraints.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II and subprocessor inventory are available; I'll push the SOC snapshot and the latest inventory after internal sign-off.
- E-sign: DocuSign is fine. We can route via DocuSign (preferred) or AdobeSign on request.

Next steps: Monica — can you take the Helix redline and provide counsel comments + mark any non-starters? I'll prepare our DPA template (attached) for side-by-side.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@helixhealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-13 02:20 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Privacy Annex — initial redlines and questions

Emma / Sean —

Thanks — I reviewed Helix_DPA_Redlines_v1 and prepared a short counsel memo (attached: Priv_Counsel_Comments_round1.pdf). Summary of positions and suggested compromises below (high level):

1) Subprocessors (Section 3.2):
- Helix asks to carve out analytics. We consider that a material operational change only if it introduces new external providers. Proposed compromise: allow analytics subprocessor use but require 30-day notice and a right to object for security/regulatory reasons; if Helix objects, we will either: (a) offer a migration/segregation plan where feasible, or (b) agree to restrict processing of Helix PII by that subprocessor.

2) Transfers & SCCs (Section 4):
- We will accept SCCs + an EU-US addendum for transfers. Recommended addendum language included in the attached redline. We cannot accept open-ended cross-border indemnities; instead, we propose audit and technical controls (encryption in transit and at rest, region pinning where contractually possible).

3) Retention (Section 6):
- Recommend numeric defaults: 7 years for customer-controlled production data; 90 days for telemetry/logs. If Helix requires 5 years for specific regulated records, we can add a schedule to Appendix A for those datasets.

4) Audit evidence & assessments:
- We will provide current SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) and a certified subprocessor inventory. We cannot share full penetration-test reports without an NDA; we can provide a short test-summary and redacted findings or execute a mutual NDA for deeper sharing.

5) Security incidents / breach notification:
- Our SLA is 72 hours initial notification + ongoing updates; we can shorten to 48 hours for High/Critical incidents on request.

6) Execution path (DocuSign):
- DocuSign is fine. Once redlines converge, we'll prepare an execution packet. Suggested flow: (a) Helix sends final redline, (b) Redwood issues counseled redline and DocuSign packet, (c) Helix legal executes via DocuSign. We can accommodate countersigning by a delegated exec if needed.

Open items for Helix to confirm: whether analytics subprocessor restriction is a hard stop, and whether Helix accepts the proposed numeric retention defaults or prefers 5 years across the board.

I've attached a redline PDF + a short counsel memo. Sean — please confirm you can post the SOC snapshot + current subprocessor inventory to the secure link below once I sign off.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Priv_Counsel_Comments_round1.pdf (pdf, 56KB)
